sources.observation: For an open mergeable pull request, the default pull_request checkout uses refs/pull/<number>/merge and GITHUB_SHA identifies the synthetic merge commit, so CI can test the proposed change combined with the target branch.

sources.topic: merge queue trigger and combined group
sources.observation: Required GitHub Actions checks used by merge queue must listen for merge_group. The queue constructs a temporary group from current base plus queued changes and merges only after required checks pass.
Repository rulesets can require status checks and merge queue; strict branch-up-to-date checks cause more branch refresh builds, while merge queue proves current combined source.
The official upload action exposes artifact ID, URL, and SHA-256 digest; current artifact generations are immutable within a workflow run.
GitHub artifact attestations can bind binary subjects to workflow, repository, commit, and event provenance when the workflow has only the documented permissions.
A GitHub environment can require reviewers, prevent self-review, restrict deployment branches or tags, and withhold environment secrets until protection rules pass.

usageBoundary: These observations constrain the proposed GitHub workflow design. Repository source and executable checks must still fail closed if the platform contract or selected action revision changes.
